notes:
K8Secret 0.6.15 — no more keychain password prompt.

If K8Secret asked you for a keychain password, this release stops it, and you can say no to any prompt you have already been given.

To present a client certificate to your cluster, macOS has to turn the certificate and key from your kubeconfig into something it can use for a handshake. The function that does this stores the result in your login keychain by default — which K8Secret was letting it do. Because K8Secret is signed without an Apple Developer account, every release carries a different signature, so macOS treated each update as a new application reaching for something the previous one had stored, and asked you to authorise it.

Nothing is stored now. The certificate is used for the handshake and exists only for as long as the app is running. On macOS 15 and later this is what the system provides for exactly this purpose; on macOS 14, which has no equivalent, K8Secret removes the item immediately after use.

If earlier versions left certificates in your keychain, you can remove them in Keychain Access — look for your cluster user's name, such as 'masterclient' or 'system:admin'.
